skill.name: kinetic-typography
skill.description: Create animated headlines, title cards, and captions with CSS, GSAP SplitText, Framer Motion, or Remotion. The recipes cover staggered reveals, variable fonts, and text on SVG paths.
skill.summary: Animate text by line, word, or character for web and video projects.
skill.author: iart-ai

security_audit.summary: The static matches are Markdown formatting, JavaScript string literals, or local animation preview instructions. Separate dependency risks arise from the unpinned Playwright command and the optional CDN script. No evidence of prompt injection, credential collection, or intentional data transfer was found.

remediation.issue: The Playwright screenshot example can execute a package version that is not pinned.
remediation.suggestion: Document how to run an approved, lockfile-pinned local Playwright installation. Offer a manual browser screenshot as the fallback.

remediation.issue: The optional GSAP CDN script has no stated version pin or integrity check.
remediation.suggestion: Default to CSS for standalone previews. Use a reviewed local GSAP asset or an exact CDN version with a subresource integrity hash.

remediation.issue: The skill advertises packaged screenshot helpers that are absent from the audited bundle.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the helper references or include the reviewed scripts in the bundle. Do not direct agents to substitute scripts from the workspace.

content.value_statement: Text reveals can become hard to read when motion, timing, and line breaks compete. Use recipes for staggered reveals, variable fonts, and frame previews to keep the text clear.
actual_capabilities: Build masked rises, blur fades, and directional wipes with CSS.
Stagger lines, words, or characters with GSAP SplitText, Framer Motion, or browser JavaScript.
Build frame-based character reveals with Remotion springs and interpolation.
Animate variable font weight or width, move text along an SVG curve, or draw an outlined stroke.
Create a standalone HTML demo with a browser time control for screenshot review.
Apply full-text accessibility labels, hide duplicate fragments, and plan a reduced-motion final state.
limitations: Framework examples require their respective libraries. The GSAP example requires GSAP 3.13 or later.
The variable font effects require a font that supports the chosen axes and ranges.
The sample CSS frame preview replaces animation delays, so staggered effects need a separate timing check.
The skill does not transcribe audio or generate lyric timestamps.

use_cases.title: Reveal a product headline
use_cases.description: Animate a two-line heading with a masked rise and keep the final text visible when reduced motion is enabled.

use_cases.title: Design a curved title card
use_cases.description: Set a title along an SVG curve and adjust spacing, type weight, and travel speed before choosing the final composition.

use_cases.title: Animate timed video captions
use_cases.description: Use supplied caption timings to plan a Remotion sequence with short character entrances and readable holds.

prompt_templates.title: Reveal one headline
prompt_templates.prompt: Animate the headline [text] with a CSS masked rise in one HTML file. Show the final headline without animation when reduced motion is enabled.
prompt_templates.scenario: A first animation with no library dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Stagger a tagline by word
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Framer Motion word reveal for [tagline]. Keep the full heading available to screen readers and check wrapping at 360 pixels.
prompt_templates.scenario: A short tagline in a React project.

prompt_templates.title: Preview a GSAP line reveal
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a masked GSAP SplitText reveal for [headline] with the project dependency. Wait for fonts, add timeline seeking, and check the first, middle, and last frames.
prompt_templates.scenario: A browser title that needs precise visual review.

prompt_templates.title: Build a timed Remotion caption sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [caption timings] and [frame rate] to build a staggered Remotion caption sequence. Keep each caption readable as a whole and show the frame calculations.
prompt_templates.scenario: A video project with prepared captions and fixed timing.

output_examples.input: Reveal a two-line headline in a standalone browser demo.
output: The first line rises inside its mask, and the second follows 80 milliseconds later.
The preview can pause at the start, midpoint, or end for inspection.
Reduced motion displays both lines in their final positions.

output_examples.input: Make a short Remotion title reveal at 60 frames per second.
output: Each character starts two frames after the previous character.
The characters rise and fade into place, then the full title holds steady.
The preview focuses on frame timing and title readability.

best_practices: Check line breaks and spacing after fonts load, then choose whether to animate lines, words, or characters.
Expose the full text to assistive technology and test the final state with reduced motion enabled.
Inspect the start, middle, and end for clipped letters, font flashes, and incorrect line breaks.
anti_patterns: Do not use long character staggers for paragraphs. Animate by word or line when the copy is long.
Do not let CSS and a GSAP timeline animate the same reveal.
Do not assume a static font can interpolate weight or width like a variable font.

faq.question: Can I make an animation without JavaScript?
faq.answer: Yes. With markup that wraps each line, CSS can handle a masked rise, blur-in, or directional wipe.

faq.question: When should I reveal by word rather than by character?
faq.answer: Use word or line reveals for longer text. Character reveals work best for short phrases where the stagger stays brief.

faq.question: Can I use this skill for video?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Remotion recipes that use frame timing and an After Effects expression example.

faq.question: Does it create captions from audio?
faq.answer: No. Provide the caption text and timings, then use the recipes to animate them.

faq.question: How can I keep split text accessible?
faq.answer: Keep the full text as the accessible heading, hide duplicate fragments from assistive technology, and test the reduced-motion state.

faq.question: Can I preview a specific moment without installing a tool?
faq.answer: Yes. Open the HTML preview in a browser and set the time in its URL if the preview includes the time control.
